content.text: {"answer":"Yes — this was already hit. The builder tried dashboard-issued org tokens (both an Admin org token and a token in a newly created 'small-deploy' org) as the worker's FLY_API_TOKEN, but `createLimitedAccessToken` rejected them: \"dashboard org tokens can't mint scoped tokens either — Fly only allows `createLimitedAccessToken` from your **user auth token**\" (m1980). The fix that worked was switching the worker's `FLY_API_TOKEN` to a Fly *user* auth token, since only that token type can mint the 1h app-scoped deploy tokens handed to the CLI (decision d5). As a side effect, since the user token also covers the existing `personal` org, deploys stayed in `personal` rather than migrating to the new org (decision d6). This matches the code: `packages/control-plane/src/fly.js` lines 1-2 note the org admin token never leaves the worker, and `mintDeployToken` (lines 48-56) calls `createLimitedAccessToken` via GraphQL using whatever `env.FLY_API_TOKEN` is configured — which must be a user token per this finding, not a dashboard org token.\n\nNext step: confirm the deployed worker's `FLY_API_TOKEN` secret is indeed a user auth token, not an org token, since a stale org-token config would reproduce this exact failure.","citations":[{"kind":"decision","decision_id":"d5"},{"kind":"message","message_id":"m1980"},{"kind":"code","path":"packages/control-plane/src/fly.js","start_line":48,"end_line":56},{"kind":"code","path":"packages/control-plane/src/fly.js","start_line":1,"end_line":2}]}
